title: The Prince and the Pauper
text:
In Mark Twain's novel, two boys are born in London on the same day in the reign of Henry VIII. One is Edward Tudor, heir to the throne. The other is Tom Canty, a beggar's son from Offal Court. They look exactly alike. When Tom wanders up to the palace gate, Prince Edward invites him in, and for fun the two trade clothes. Before the prince can explain, the guards throw him out into the street in Tom's rags.

No one believes Edward is the prince. He is beaten by Tom's father, falls among thieves and beggars, and wanders the country. A discharged soldier, Miles Hendon, takes pity on the boy, thinks him mad, and protects him anyway. On the road Edward sees what the king's laws do to the poor: he is thrown into jail, meets two women who are burned at the stake for their religion, and hears of people hanged for stealing small things to eat. He promises himself that the law will change.

Meanwhile Henry VIII dies, and Tom is about to be crowned. At the very moment of the coronation, Edward pushes into the abbey. He proves who he is by revealing where the missing Great Seal is hidden; Tom has been using it to crack nuts. Crowned at last, Edward VI rules with mercy, rewards Tom and Miles Hendon, and often tells stories of what he saw on the road.
lesson: Rules look different from the receiving end. If you make decisions for others, find ways to experience what your choices are like for the people with the least power.
people: Edward Tudor (Edward VI), Tom Canty, Miles Hendon
source: Mark Twain, The Prince and the Pauper, 1881
